assign.request: Reviewer minion for /imagine/decks/: ten-second test, primary interaction, layout at 3440, resolve findings in-realm, land.

log.msg: Ten-second test (before fix), 1280 + 3440 shots of /imagine/decks/. Stranger sentence: a gallery of ten small ratio diagrams (Half, Golden, Aside, Triptych, Poster, Four, Persistent, Swap, The pitch) captioned in vocabulary that assumes you already know what a screen region or a slide cut is - reads like an internal design-system exhibit, not something with an obvious next action. Meant sentence (readme.md + description): nine presentational layouts for cutting a screen into regions, studying which content survives which region shape. Matches paging/critique's decks row exactly: 41% wide, 1856px dead, depth 7, scroll 2105/1392, weak='Ten ratio-lab cards stack in a narrow column, and the intro prose alone overflows about 713px past the fold', alt='Tile wall, wide, plus an expand disclosure on the long intro instead of a flat scroll', score 77. The alternate had NOT been applied before this task - page.js still had width:'large' (28-64em cap) and an inline comment acknowledging the dead .md doc-link trap without fixing it.

Fix 1 (highest-value, the missing/author's-vocabulary takeaway sentence): page.js's opening sentence rewritten in plain words - 'Nine ways to cut one screen into pieces, the way a slide splits into a picture and a caption. Each card below is a real page - click one to open it full-screen and see that cut built with real text and shapes in it, not a diagram.' The old opening ('Slide-grade layouts... once you have the screen, how do you cut it, and what kind of content survives the piece it lands in') led with three undefined-in-place terms (screen/cut/piece). Kept the /imagine/screens/ cross-link and the golden-ratio measurement paragraph as the technical detail underneath, per 'clear beats brief': plain sentence first, jargon after, nothing deleted. Caveat: 'piece' and 'cut' are still this lab's working nouns everywhere else (readme, deck.js, doc/regions.md) - I defined them in the lead sentence instead of replacing them, so the vocabulary stays consistent across the realm; undo if the owner would rather rename the concept itself.

Fix 2 (layout, matches paging/critique's decks row exactly - 41% wide, 1856px dead, alt 'Tile wall, wide'): page.js width changed 'large' (28-64em cap) to 'fill'. Verified this is the same qualifying case as blogx/page.js (established finding): every one of decks' nine children is a Deck whose column() defaults to (or explicitly sets) width:'full', so no third column ever opens beside this index in the /imagine/ row - 'fill's neighbours-keep-their-floor behaviour is exactly the documented case for it (doc/columns.md). 'full' itself was not tried: it would collapse /imagine/'s own hub rail, the same regression gallery reverted 2026-08-29. Measured live at 3440 after the fix: the previews wall (already a real grid/'Tile wall' via core's previews()+bleed, not a plain link list) now spans 2910px of the 3440 row (x:480, right edge ~3390, vs the page's own gutter) and lays 6 cards per row instead of 4; the hub rail and the crumb strip both survive untouched at 1280 and 3440. Paragraphs and the content-kind table stay capped at the 40em measure (they are plain .page children, not .bleed), so no line runs past the measure - the wall alone got wider, exactly as the 'four of five kinds scale, prose never should' finding says. Caveat: did NOT add a separate expand/disclosure on the intro prose (the critique's other suggested half-fix) - two short paragraphs is not what was overflowing; widening the wall already cut total page height roughly in half by letting groups of 6/2/1 cards sit in far fewer rows. Undo (back to width:'large') only if a future child page ever needs to open as a real sibling column instead of going full-screen.

Fix 3 (dead doc links, the established finding - Router never intercepts an extension link): added public/imagine/decks/doc/page.js, a route() shim copied from blogx/doc/page.js's pattern, giving doc/regions.md and doc/decisions.md real pretty urls (/imagine/decks/doc/regions/, /imagine/decks/doc/decisions/). Updated the three link sites that pointed at the raw .md file: page.js's closing paragraph (which had an inline comment admitting the trap without fixing it) and readme.md's five self-links (map line, decisions-table line, Watch-out x2, More x2). Verified live: both pretty urls 200, render as styled Miller-columns content (not raw markdown), zero console errors; clicking through from the rendered /imagine/decks/readme/ page confirmed all self-links now resolve to the pretty form. Caveat: left readme.md's ONE cross-realm link to /imagine/screens/doc/decisions.md as-is - that destination has no doc/page.js route yet, so pointing it at a pretty url would 404 outright instead of loading raw markdown; fixing it needs a doc/page.js in the screens/ realm, outside my fences (proposed below, not fixed).

Primary interaction verified via ui-test drive.mjs (scratchpad decks-plan.json, decks-ui2/steps.json, 18 steps, zero console errors on every step): clicking the first card (Half) navigates to /imagine/decks/half/, title 'Half', a real full-screen 50/50 slide with live text ('Peers' / 'Or nothing') appears - not a diagram. ArrowRight then advances to /imagine/decks/golden/ (deck.js's neighbor() order, matches the footer strip's own 1/6..6/6 count). Clicking the footer ring's own chip (href=/imagine/decks/aside/) navigates there directly, title 'Aside' - the strip is a set of real links, not a fake nav. Trap hit and fixed while building the plan: a click selector split on the descendant-combinator SPACE ('.page--decks a...') silently used only the first token per SKILL.md's documented trap, clicking the wrong ancestor and landing on the wrong slide first try; switched to single-token href-attribute selectors (a.page-preview-link[href=...], a.decks-chip[href=...]) and it worked cleanly on the second run. Not a skill gap - SKILL.md already names this exact trap under Verbs; no improvements.md entry needed, just my own miss on the first pass.

Proposal (not fixed - lives in a sibling realm, outside my fences): readme.md's one cross-realm link to /imagine/screens/doc/decisions.md is still a bare .md href (the general dead-doc-link finding). The fix is the same shim I just built here, applied to /imagine/screens/: add public/imagine/screens/doc/page.js with a route('decisions') returning md.file(meta,'decisions.md',{h1:false}), then repoint any screens/page.js or readme.md links at /imagine/screens/doc/decisions/. One file, ~15 lines, copy of this task's own doc/page.js - belongs to the screens/ reviewer, not to me.

Re-shot 1280 + 3440 after all three fixes: zero console errors on every shot (index at both sizes, half/, golden/, doc/regions/). Final jpeg for the manager's shots/ dir: quality 70, 83.6KB (150KB cap).

assign.outcome:
**Decks' landing page went from an author-vocabulary opening and a `large` column wasting 1856px at 3440 (paging/critique: 41% wide, score 77) to a plain-language takeaway sentence and a card wall that fills 2910 of 3440px in six columns.** Two dead doc links are now real urls. Stranger test now passes: `/imagine/decks/`.

- Fixed `page.js`: opening sentence rewritten in plain words - 'Nine ways to cut one screen into pieces, the way a slide splits into a picture and a caption. Each card below is a real page - click one to open it full-screen...' - replacing an opener that led with three undefined terms (screen/cut/piece). `width: "large"` (28-64em cap) changed to `"fill"`, the same qualifying pattern as `blogx/page.js`: every one of decks' nine children escapes to its own full-screen `Deck`, so nothing ever opens as a third column beside this index - verified live, hub rail and crumb strip both survive at 1280 and 3440.
- Added `doc/page.js` (copied from `blogx/doc/page.js`'s pattern): `doc/regions.md` and `doc/decisions.md` now have real urls, `/imagine/decks/doc/regions/` and `/imagine/decks/doc/decisions/`, fixing the dead-link trap (`Router` never intercepts an extension link) called out in `page.js`'s own old comment, which had named the trap without closing it. Updated all five self-links in `readme.md` and the one in `page.js` to the pretty form; left the realm's one cross-realm link (`/imagine/screens/doc/decisions.md`) alone and proposed the same fix for that realm below.
- Verified the primary interaction end to end (`ui-test drive.mjs`, 18 steps, zero console errors on every step): clicking the Half card opens a real full-screen 50/50 slide with live text; `ArrowRight` advances to Golden; the footer ring's own chips are real links (clicked straight to Aside). Hit and fixed SKILL.md's own documented space-splitting trap while building the plan - not a skill gap, just my own miss on the first pass.
- Proposed, not fixed (screens/ realm, outside my fences): give `/imagine/screens/` the same `doc/page.js` shim so its own `doc/decisions.md` link stops being a raw-markdown full-page-load.
